consensus_summary: Primary identification is the Christological title for Jesus as the reliable testifier to God's truth (even unto death), drawn chiefly from Rev 1:5 and 3:14; complementary alternatives include ecclesial martyrs and the Psalm 89:37 celestial/covenantal witness (moon or heavens).
book_summary: The Messiah who faithfully bears the Father's light through the night, with the moon writing this witness in the sky.
consensus_core_identification: Jesus Christ / the Messiah as faithful witness
book_core_identification: The Messiah as faithful witness (expressed via lunar imagery)
boundary_disagreement: Book elevates and fuses the Psalm 89 moon imagery as the definitional mode by which the Messiah's witness is written in the sky, whereas consensus keeps the moon as a minority/rare alternative reading of the Psalm phrase itself, separate from the primary Christological title.
rationale: Minimum cores both fix on the Messiah/Christ as the referent of the title, so no replacement occurs. The book preserves that central identification while materially tightening precision and reclassifying the celestial imagery from a detachable OT background or alternative into an intrinsic symbolic mechanism ('the moon writes this witness'), producing a refined boundary rather than equivalence or contradiction.
strongest_objection: The book's seamless merger of Messiah and moon could be read as shifting the primary referent toward the celestial sign rather than merely illustrating the Christological title.
